scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The style grew out of the Lindy Hop around 1920, evolving through 1940s Boogie Woogie.
By 1955, as rock music swept in, the movement shifted toward a competitive, acrobatic discipline.
In the 1970s, French dance schools in Lyon formalized the sport, leading to the creation of the World Rock'N'Roll Confederation, or WRRC.
on_screen: Map: United States (origin), France (modern sport development) · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is primarily a competitive sport.
It is performed at local, national, and international championships organized by the WRRC.
The focus is on precision, athleticism, and the successful execution of high-difficulty acrobatic elements.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The footwork builds on a six-basic or nine-basic step structure.
The nine-basic step serves as the modern tournament standard, built around a kick-ball-change.
Dancers travel along linear paths, holding an upright posture while firing kicks into the air.
Watch for specialized moves like the Einsteiger and the Körperwelle.

Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Linear movement, pairs or formation groups.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Couples dance in 4/4 time, moving to modern disco or pop tracks set between 176 and 208 beats per minute.
The accent lands on the first and third beats of every measure, unlike classic off-beat rock.
Listen to the modern pop and disco instrumentation.
The core pulse holds a steady 4/4 meter at roughly 192 beats per minute.
This high-tempo driving beat delivers a clear pulse to power rapid footwork and airborne acrobatics.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear custom-made, multicoloured costumes crafted from elastic, durable artificial fibers.
These are designed to be tight-fitting to prevent snagging during acrobatics.
Footwear consists of light jazz shoes for dance programs or aerobics sneakers for acrobatic programs to provide grip and shock absorption.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Notable figures include French world champion Miguel Angueira and Katerina Tikhonova, who has competed in the sport.
Categories are divided by age and skill level, including Youth, Juniors, and Main Class (Contact Style and Free Style).
Swing (1920s) -> Lindy Hop -> Boogie Woogie (1940s) -> Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll (1955-present).

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll traces its lineage to Lindy Hop, the 1920s swing dance that first introduced aerial elements.
It also stems from Boogie Woogie, a faster swing adaptation that linked original social dance to rock music.
